prompt: Starting in a deep crouch, the dancer places both hands on the floor. They kick their legs out behind them to a plank position, then quickly jump their feet back toward their hands. They explode upward, leaping straight into the air with arms reaching fully toward the ceiling.

The dancer stands on one leg while the other leg is tucked with the foot at the knee. They slowly rotate their entire body to the right. Both arms are held in a soft circle in front of the chest throughout the entire slow turn.

With feet close together, the dancer slides their right foot back while the left heel lifts. As the right foot reaches far back, they quickly switch feet, sliding the left foot back. This creates a smooth backpedaling motion while the arms swing naturally at the sides.

The dancer leans their torso far to the left while extending the right arm over their head. They sweep the right arm in a wide circle down toward the floor and up again. As the arm rises, the torso follows until the body is standing upright again.

Standing firmly, the dancer kicks the right leg forward and snaps the left arm across the waist. The torso twists sharply to the right while the head remains facing forward. The body then lunges onto the left leg, sweeping both arms in a wide arc over the head.

The body begins in a crouch. The dancer hops onto the balls of the feet, crossing the right ankle over the left. Simultaneously, the arms cross at the wrists in front of the chest. The feet jump wide apart as the arms explode outward into a high V-shape.

The dancer raises the right knee high while the left arm swings forward and the right arm pulls back. Releasing the leg, the person performs a series of small, rapid steps backward on the toes. The upper body remains rigid while the head tilts slightly side to side.

Starting with feet together, the dancer slides the right foot out into a wide stance. The torso leans low toward the right knee while the left arm reaches toward the opposite wall. The body then rolls upward through the spine, ending with the chest pressed forward.

The performer stands with feet together then steps the right foot out wide while the right arm sweeps a low arc. The torso leans left as the left arm reaches toward the ceiling. They pull both elbows into the ribs while jumping to bring the feet back together.

Starting in a deep crouch, the dancer thrusts their chest forward and pulls the shoulders back. They step back on the left foot while the right arm punches toward the floor. The head snaps to the right as they drag the right foot across the ground to close.

The body stands tall with arms reaching overhead. The right leg lifts into a side kick while the torso tilts left to balance. As the leg lowers, the dancer performs a rapid spin to the right on the balls of the feet with arms tucked into the chest.

The dancer begins on one knee with the opposite leg extended behind. They push off the floor to stand, sweeping both arms upward in a circular path. They step forward with the left foot, sinking into a deep lunge while the right arm reaches forward and down.

The torso leans forward while the hips sway toward the right. The hands rest on the thighs as the dancer steps the left foot back and then forwards. They straighten the spine and raise both hands rapidly toward the chin before spreading the arms wide and low.

From a squat, the body leaps upward while the arms swing wide to the sides. The legs tuck toward the chest at the peak of the jump. After landing softly on both feet, the torso leans forward and the right arm sweeps across the floor in a semi-circle.

The dancer stands on the left leg while the right knee lifts high. The right foot then strikes the ground firmly. Both arms pump up and down at the sides with bent elbows, followed by a quick shift of weight as the hips sway toward the right side.

Starting with feet together, the left leg slides out to the side while the torso tilts the opposite way. Both arms extend fully above the head. The dancer then pulls the left foot back in, bending both knees into a deep crouch while the arms drop to the shins.

The upper body leans back as the right leg kicks forward with a straight knee. The arms reach out in front of the chest. Stepping forward onto the right foot, the body rotates to the right, arms pulling tight to the torso before expanding outward to the sides.

The dancer balances on the balls of the feet, stepping rapidly in place. The arms are held straight out at shoulder height. The torso shimmies back and forth with quick, small vibrations while the head remains steady and the gaze stays focused forward.

The dancer stands with feet together then steps the left foot wide while sweeping the right arm across the chest. The hips shift right as the left arm reaches high. The body rotates toward the right side while the arms drop and the knees bend deeply into a squat.

From a standing position the dancer lifts the right knee high toward the chest while the left arm reaches forward. The right foot steps back firmly as the torso leans forward. Both arms sweep in a broad circle toward the left before the body returns to a neutral upright stance.

The dancer stands on the balls of the feet with arms rounded in front. They step forward with the right foot and extend the left leg straight back into the air. The torso leans forward as the arms open wide to the sides for balance before the back leg lowers.

The dancer stands with feet together then steps the right leg out wide into a deep bend. Both arms sweep from the floor upward to the ceiling. The head follows the hands as the body stretches tall and the heels lift off the ground.

Starting from a crouch, the person thrusts the right leg forward while leaning the torso back. The arms pump back and forth at the sides. They quickly pull the leg back and jump into the air, landing with feet wide and knees bent.

The dancer stands on the left leg while the right leg extends forward with a pointed foot. The left arm reaches forward and the right arm opens to the side. They smoothly rotate the body to the right while keeping the right leg raised.

The person stands tall and steps forward with the right foot, then crosses the left foot behind. They turn their entire body to the right until facing forward again. During the turn, the arms pull inward toward the chest and then extend outward.

The performer stands with feet together then steps the right foot out wide while the right arm sweeps across the chest. The body sinks into a deep squat as the left arm reaches towards the sky. Both hands then clasp together and pull sharply toward the right hip.

The body begins in a crouch with palms flat on the floor. Rapidly, the dancer kicks the legs out into a plank position before pulling the knees back toward the chest. Standing quickly, the person jumps into the air with arms tucked tight against the ribcage.

Starting from a neutral stance, the dancer lifts the right knee high while the left arm pushes forward. The right leg then extends straight back as the torso leans forward to form a horizontal line. The arms reach outward to the sides for balance before returning upright.

The dancer stands on the balls of the feet and takes small, rapid steps backward. While moving, the arms ripple in a wave motion starting from the right fingertips, across the shoulders, and out through the left hand. The head tilts slightly toward the trailing shoulder.

Starting from a crouched position, the dancer thrusts their chest forward and snaps their head back. They rise to a full stand while rolling their shoulders backward in a rhythmic sequence. The right leg kicks out low to the front as the opposite arm punches toward the ground.

The person balances on their left leg while the right knee lifts high toward the chest. Both arms circle outward and upward until the palms meet above the head. They step down firmly, rotating the entire torso to the left while keeping the arms parallel to the floor.

The dancer slides their right foot across the floor into a wide stance. Both hands press forward as if pushing a wall. They execute a quick turn to the right on the balls of their feet, ending with the left arm curved over the head and the right arm behind.

Standing with feet side by side, the person bounces their knees rhythmically. The right hand taps the left shoulder, then the left hand taps the right shoulder. They lean the torso back while sliding both feet backward in small, smooth increments while the arms swing loosely.

The dancer stands with feet together, then steps out wide with the right leg while crossing arms over the chest. They pull the elbows back sharply, then slide the left foot to meet the right while the head tilts toward the shoulder.

Starting from a crouch, the dancer thrusts the chest forward and flings both arms wide. They spring upward, tucking the knees toward the torso, and land softly on the balls of the feet with knees bent and arms reaching toward the ceiling.

The body balances on the left leg while the right leg lifts, bending at the knee. The dancer rotates the entire body toward the right, sweeping the left arm in a horizontal arc while the right arm stays tucked against the waist.

The dancer steps forward with the right foot, then pivots the hips to the left. As they turn, both arms ripple from the shoulders down to the fingertips in a wave motion, finishing with the left leg extended straight back.

The dancer stands with feet together then steps the right foot wide. The hips circle to the right and back while the arms reach upward. As the hips complete the circle, the body drops into a deep squat with hands touching the floor before springing back to a standing position.

The body stands tall with arms extended to the sides. The right leg lifts with a bent knee while the torso tilts left. The lifted leg sweeps in a wide arc to the back as the arms move downward to cross at the wrists, ending in a stable forward lunge.

The dancer steps forward with the left foot and executes a sharp turn to the right on the balls of the feet. During the turn, the arms pull tightly into the chest. As the turn finishes, the arms fly outward and the chest pushes forward with a rhythmic bounce.

Standing with feet parallel, the dancer waves their right arm from the fingertips through the elbow and shoulder across the chest. The motion transfers to the left shoulder and flows down the left arm. Simultaneously, the knees bend and straighten in a fluid, continuous pulsing motion.

The dancer starts in a deep squat with arms crossed at the wrists. They jump upward, extending both legs wide and flinging their arms out to the sides. Upon landing, they slide the right foot behind the left and pivot on their toes to face the opposite direction.

The body leans forward with the right arm reaching toward the floor. The left leg kicks back and up into the air. The dancer pulls the leg down, tucks the chin, and performs a smooth roll across the shoulders before standing up with arms stretched towards the sky.

Starting with a straight spine, the dancer steps forward with the left foot and bends both knees deeply. They rotate the torso to the right while sweeping the right arm in a wide circle. The heels lift high as the body turns quickly on the balls of the feet.

The dancer balances on the left leg while the right foot rests against the inner knee. Both arms curve upward to form an oval above the head. They slowly lower the right foot, step to the side, and tilt the head toward the shoulder while extending the palms outward.

Starting from a crouched position, the body springs upward while the right leg kicks straight to the side. Both arms reach toward the ceiling. Upon landing on both feet, the torso leans forward and the elbows pull back sharply toward the hips.

The dancer stands on the left leg while the right knee lifts high toward the chest. The left arm reaches forward and the right arm extends back. They switch legs rapidly, pumping the arms in opposition while maintaining a steady rhythmic bounce through the ankles.

The torso tilts deeply to the left side while the right arm arches over the head. The right leg slides outward along the floor until fully extended. The body then pulls back to center, drawing the feet together and bringing both hands to the chest.

From a standing position, the right foot steps behind the left while the hips sway toward the right. The arms flow in a wide circle across the front of the body. The feet cross and uncross rapidly as the dancer travels sideways with small steps.

The body drops into a wide squat with the spine vertical. The hands rest on the knees before one shoulder rolls forward and then the other. The dancer stands up quickly, throwing the head back and extending the arms wide to the sides.

First, the body lowers into a deep squat to store energy while both arms swing behind the torso, then the legs extend with extreme force to drive the body into a vertical leap. At this point, the arms swing rapidly upward toward the ceiling to maximize momentum before the body returns to the ground, landing with the knees bending to absorb impact while the torso remains upright to stabilize.

The body leans forward while one leg tucks under the torso to prepare for a sprint start, then the legs drive off an invisible starting block with a sudden burst of speed. At this point, the arms swing in a wide, rhythmic motion to pull the torso forward while the legs cycle through powerful strides. Finally, the body transitions into a steady upright posture, maintaining a smooth running motion to keep balance.

First, the body lowers into a deep crouch while the arms swing far back to store energy, then the legs drive powerfully against the floor to propel the body into a high vertical leap. At this point, the arms swing rapidly upward toward the ceiling to add momentum while the torso remains upright. Finally, the legs extend to meet the ground and bend upon impact, with the arms moving to the sides to ensure a stable landing.

The body leans forward while the legs bend deeply to build tension, then the legs explode backward as if pushing off starting blocks to initiate a rapid sprint. During this phase, the arms pump vigorously forward and backward while the torso remains inclined to maintain acceleration. Finally, the body transitions into an upright posture as the legs continue their high-speed cycle, with the arms maintaining a steady rhythm to provide balance.

First, the body lowers into a squat position with the torso tilted forward and arms held near the chest as if gripping an invisible heavy ball, then the legs and torso extend rapidly to launch the invisible object into the air. At this point, the arms thrust forcefully upward and forward to complete the throwing motion. Finally, the body lands firmly on both feet while the arms drop back to the sides to regain a steady standing position.

The body starts in a plank position and then lowers the torso toward the floor to coil the muscles, followed by an explosive push that launches the upper body off the ground. At this point, the arms fully extend and the hands leave the surface to perform a quick clap in mid-air before returning to the floor. Finally, the arms bend to absorb the impact of the descent while the legs and torso remain rigid to stabilize the landing.

First, the body lowers into a deep crouch to store energy, with the torso leaning forward and arms pulled back. Then, the legs explode upward in a powerful vertical leap, while the arms swing forcefully toward the ceiling to drive the body into the air. Finally, the body lands on the balls of the feet with the knees bending to absorb the impact, while the arms extend to the sides to maintain a stable standing position.

The body begins in a plank position with the weight distributed between the hands and feet. Then, the arms push off the ground with such force that the upper body is propelled upward, while the torso remains rigid to transfer energy efficiently. Finally, the hands return to the ground to catch the body's weight, and the arms bend slightly to cushion the descent and return to a stable starting posture.

First, the person squats deeply with the torso leaning forward and arms extended toward the ground as if gripping an invisible heavy bar, then the legs drive upward with immense force while the torso snaps upright and the arms pull the invisible weight toward the chest. At this point, the arms finish by pushing the invisible bar rapidly toward the ceiling while the legs extend fully, and finally, the body drops slightly into a quarter-squat to catch the weight before standing tall to a stable position.

First, the body crouches low with the legs staggered and the torso almost horizontal to the ground to prepare for a sudden burst, then the legs push off with maximum force to propel the body forward into a high-speed sprint while the arms pump vigorously by the sides. At this point, the head stays aligned with the forward-tilting torso to maintain aerodynamic efficiency as the legs cycle rapidly to increase velocity, and finally, the stride length shortens and the torso rises to a vertical position to decelerate into a stable stop.

The body first bends forward at the waist with the knees slightly flexed and arms swinging far behind the torso to build momentum, then the legs explode upward and backward while the torso arches into the air to perform a backflip. At this point, the arms swing forward and then tuck toward the knees to accelerate the rotation of the torso and legs through the air, and finally, the legs extend toward the ground to absorb the impact upon landing while the arms reach forward to maintain a centered balance.

First, the body stands with left leg raised high and the arms drawn back to the chest to concentrate energy in the core, then the supporting right leg drives into the ground as the raised left leg thrusts forward and upward in a powerful kick against an invisible barrier. At this point, the torso leans slightly backward to counter the force of the leg while the arms snap downward to provide stability and leverage for the strike, and finally, the kicking left leg is pulled back quickly and placed firmly on the ground to return the body to a steady upright posture.

First, the body crouches deeply into a squat with the torso leaning forward and arms swung far behind the back to store energy, then the legs drive powerfully into the ground to propel the body upward and backward into the air. At this point, the torso arches back while the arms swing overhead to provide momentum for a full rotation, and finally, the legs extend to meet the ground while the torso straightens and the arms reach forward to stabilize the landing.

The body stands with the left side facing forward, torso twisted to the right rear to build tension. The arms mimic holding an invisible shot put, extending over the head and slightly bending behind the back. The weight quickly shifts from the back leg to the front leg, and the torso rotates forward with high speed. The arms snap forward to simulate throwing an invisible shot put, fully extending to release energy. Finally, the rear leg swings across the body, and the arms drop to the sides to absorb the momentum and restore balance.

First, the body tenses in a low lunge with the torso angled toward the ground and the arms positioned for a quick start, then the legs explode into a series of rapid, powerful strides to gain maximum forward acceleration. At this point, the arms pump vigorously back and forth to drive the legs further while the torso remains leaned forward to maintain momentum, and finally, the legs slow their pace into shorter steps as the torso rises to a vertical position and the arms move to the sides to steady the body.

The body first crouches low into a deep squat while the arms swing far backward and the torso leans forward to store potential energy. Then, the legs explode upward and backward in a powerful thrust as the body rotates mid-air to complete a backflip, with the arms pulling toward the chest to increase rotation speed. Finally, the legs extend toward the ground to absorb the impact, and the arms reach forward to stabilize the torso in an upright standing position.

The body starts in a standing position, then quickly drops as the palms move toward the imaginary floor and the legs kick back into a plank position. Immediately, the legs snap back toward the torso to transition into a squat, followed by an explosive jump where the arms reach toward the ceiling. Finally, the body lands softly on the balls of the feet with the torso upright to regain balance.

The torso leans slightly forward as one leg lunges backward and the opposite arm swings forward to gather tension. Suddenly, the back leg drives forward and upward into a high knee lift while the supporting leg jumps off the ground, with both arms swapping positions rapidly to generate upward speed. Finally, the body lands on the starting leg and the torso stabilizes to prevent swaying.

First, the body lowers into a deep squat while the arms reach toward the ground as if preparing to push off an invisible surface, then the legs thrust powerfully upward to initiate a high jump while the arms swing overhead to gain height. At this point, the knees tuck toward the chest at the peak of the leap before the legs extend back down to the floor. Finally, the body lands with the knees bent to absorb the impact while the torso remains upright and the arms move to the sides to maintain a stable standing position.

The body starts in a standing position before rapidly dropping the torso forward and placing the arms on the ground to kick the legs backward into a straight line, mimicking a sudden transition to a horizontal posture. Then, the legs quickly snap forward toward the chest as the torso lifts, and the entire body explodes upward into a vertical jump with the arms reaching toward the sky. Finally, the body returns to the ground with the legs slightly bent and the torso centered to regain a balanced stance.

First, the body shifts the weight onto one leg while the other leg lifts slightly and the arms move to the opposite side to wind up, then the torso rotates forcefully as the lifted leg snaps forward and out in a rapid arc to perform a roundhouse kick against an invisible target. At this point, the standing leg remains firm while the arms swing in the opposite direction of the kick to provide counter-balance and power. Finally, the kicking leg is pulled back quickly to the starting position and the torso squares up to maintain a steady defensive posture.

The body begins in a lunge position with one leg forward and the other leg back while the arms are bent at the sides, then the legs push off the ground simultaneously to launch the body into the air. At this point, the positions of the legs switch rapidly in mid-air so the back leg moves forward and the forward leg moves back, while the arms pump vigorously to assist the transition. Finally, the body lands softly with the feet in their new positions and the torso held straight to ensure a stable and controlled recovery.

First, the body stands with the feet together and the arms at the sides before suddenly jumping the legs outward to the sides while the arms swing upward in a wide arc above the head. Then, without a pause, the legs snap back together with immense speed as the arms are pulled forcefully down to the torso to reset the motion. Finally, the body absorbs the quick movement by keeping the knees flexible and the head level, ensuring the posture remains upright and ready for the next burst of energy.

First, the body lowers into a deep squat while the arms swing behind the torso to store potential energy, then the legs drive powerfully into the ground to propel the entire body into a high vertical leap. At this point, the arms swing vigorously upward to assist the elevation while the legs fully extend. Finally, the body descends and lands with the knees bent to absorb impact, with the arms moving forward to maintain a stable and balanced upright stance.

First, the body leans forward slightly with the weight shifted to the balls of the feet while the arms are poised at the sides, then the legs begin a rapid alternating drive where the knees are pulled toward the chest in an explosive sprinting motion. At this point, the arms swing forcefully forward and backward in coordination with the legs to maximize speed and momentum. Finally, the body decelerates smoothly while the legs wide-set and the torso remains upright to regain a controlled posture.

From a standing posture, the feet are placed apart with both knees slightly bent. The right arm is initially bent and held close to the right side of the body, with the right fist positioned in front of the chest. As the motion begins, the right arm extends forward along the centerline of the body, with the elbow gradually straightening and the fist facing forward. At the same time, the left arm retracts backward, with the elbow drawing in toward the left side of the torso and the left fist returning to a guarded position. The upper body remains upright, producing only a slight forward shift as the right arm extends. The motion ends with the right arm fully extended and briefly held still.

The body stands upright with both arms bent and held in front of the torso. As the motion begins, the left leg remains on the ground to support the body while the right knee lifts forward, raising the thigh to a horizontal position. Next, the lower right leg extends forward, kicking straight ahead with the right foot. Throughout the kick, the upper body remains vertical and the arms stay in a guarded position without swinging. The motion ends as the right leg retracts along the same path and the right foot returns to the ground, restoring a stable standing posture.

From a standing position, the left foot stays planted on the ground while the right leg hangs naturally. The motion begins as the torso rotates to the left and the right leg lifts off the ground. The right leg then swings outward at a horizontal level, with the lower leg extending to form a curved kicking path through the air. At the same time, both arms extend in the opposite direction of the kick to maintain balance. The motion finishes as the right leg quickly retracts and returns to the ground, and the torso rotates back to face forward.

The body stands with both feet placed firmly apart, and both arms bent in front of the torso. As the motion begins, the left arm extends forward, pushing the palm outward while the elbow gradually straightens. At the same time, the right arm retracts backward and stays close to the right side of the body in a defensive position. The upper body remains upright, with only a small forward shift accompanying the left arm’s push. The motion ends with the left arm fully extended and briefly held in place.

From a standing posture, both arms hang naturally at the sides of the body. As the motion begins, the right arm lifts quickly and moves horizontally across the right side of the body, forming a blocking position in front of the chest with the forearm held level. At the same time, the left arm retracts downward and rests close to the abdomen. The torso remains facing forward without noticeable rotation. The motion ends with the right arm held firmly in the blocking position.

From a standing posture, both arms are bent and held in front of the body. First, the right arm extends forward to perform a straight punch while the left arm retracts backward. Next, the right arm pulls back to a guarded position as the right knee lifts forward. Then, the right leg extends into a forward kick and quickly retracts. Finally, both feet settle back into a stable stance, and both arms return to a guarded position in front of the torso.

The body stands upright with both feet placed apart. Both arms are bent, with the hands held in front of the chest. As the motion begins, the left arm moves outward to the left side, opening the guard, while the right arm simultaneously extends forward into a straight punch. The torso remains facing forward without rotation. After the punch reaches full extension, the right arm retracts and both arms return to a guarded position in front of the body.

From a stable standing posture, both arms are bent at the elbows. The motion begins as the left arm moves downward across the front of the body, with the forearm angled toward the ground in a blocking position. At the same time, the right arm stays bent near the chest. After the block is established, the right arm extends forward into a short straight strike while the left arm retracts toward the torso. The motion ends with both arms returning to a guarded posture.

The body stands upright with both arms bent in front of the torso. As the motion begins, the right knee lifts upward and slightly outward while the left leg remains planted on the ground. Next, the right leg extends sideways, pushing the foot outward at hip height. During the kick, the torso stays upright and the arms remain fixed in a defensive position. The motion ends as the right leg retracts and the right foot returns to the ground.

From a standing position, both arms hang loosely at the sides. As the motion begins, both arms lift upward and cross in front of the chest, with the right forearm positioned above the left forearm. The elbows remain bent and close to the body. The torso stays facing forward without turning. After briefly holding the crossed position, both arms separate and return to a neutral guarded stance.

The body stands upright with both arms bent near the torso. As the motion begins, the left foot steps forward while the right arm extends forward into a straight punch. The left arm retracts slightly and stays close to the body. The torso remains upright and aligned with the forward step. The motion ends as the right arm retracts and the body returns to a stable standing position.

From a standing posture, both arms are raised with the elbows bent and the forearms positioned in front of the face. As the motion begins, both arms move downward in a controlled manner, lowering the guard to chest height. The elbows remain bent and close to the torso throughout the motion. The legs remain still and the torso stays upright. The motion ends with both arms held steadily in a low guarded position.

The body stands upright with both feet placed apart. Both arms are bent in front of the torso. The motion begins as the left arm extends forward into a straight strike while the right arm retracts toward the right side of the torso. After the left arm reaches full extension, it pulls back as the right arm immediately extends forward into a straight strike. The motion ends with both arms bent and held in a guarded position.

From a standing posture, both arms hang naturally at the sides. As the motion begins, the right arm lifts upward and angles inward across the front of the chest, forming a diagonal blocking position. At the same time, the left arm bends and stays close to the lower torso. The torso remains upright throughout. The motion finishes with the right arm held steadily across the chest.

The body stands upright with both arms bent near the chest. The motion begins as the right knee lifts forward while the left leg remains planted. As the knee reaches its highest position, the right leg extends forward into a controlled kick. After the extension, the right leg retracts and lowers back to the ground. The motion ends with the body returning to a stable standing posture.

From a stable standing position, both arms are raised and bent in front of the upper torso. As the motion begins, both arms move outward to the sides, opening the chest. Immediately after, both arms sweep inward and cross in front of the torso. The torso remains facing forward without rotation. The motion ends with the arms crossed briefly before returning to a guarded position.

The body stands with both feet apart and both arms bent in front of the torso. The motion begins as the torso rotates slightly to the right while the left arm extends forward at chest height. The right arm retracts toward the right side of the body. After the extension, the left arm pulls back and the torso returns to face forward. The motion ends in a stable guarded stance.

From a standing posture, the right arm hangs at the side and the left arm is bent near the torso. As the motion begins, the right arm lifts upward along the right side of the body and then sweeps downward across the front of the torso. At the same time, the left arm stays bent and close to the body. The torso remains upright. The motion ends with the right arm lowered in front of the body.

The body stands upright with both arms bent in front of the chest. The motion begins as the left leg steps slightly forward while the right leg remains behind. At the same time, the right arm extends forward into a straight strike and the left arm retracts. After the strike, the right arm pulls back and the left foot returns to its original position. The motion ends with both arms held in guard.

From a standing position, both arms hang loosely at the sides. As the motion begins, both arms lift upward to shoulder height, with the elbows bent and forearms angled inward. After briefly holding this position, both arms lower back down in front of the torso. The legs remain still throughout. The motion ends with the arms resting in a neutral guarded posture.

The body stands upright with both feet planted firmly. The motion begins as the left arm moves downward across the front of the torso, forming a low blocking position. At the same time, the right arm remains bent near the chest. After the block is established, the left arm retracts while the right arm extends forward into a straight strike. The motion ends with both arms returning to a guarded stance.

From a standing posture, both arms are bent and held in front of the torso. As the motion begins, the torso rotates to the left while the right arm extends diagonally forward. The left arm retracts toward the left side of the body. After the extension, the right arm pulls back and the torso rotates back to face forward. The motion ends with both arms bent in guard.

The body stands upright with both arms bent near the torso. As the motion begins, the right leg lifts sideways while the left leg remains planted. The right leg then extends outward into a side kick. During the kick, the torso stays upright and the arms remain fixed in front of the body. The motion ends as the right leg retracts and returns to the ground.

From a stable standing position, both arms hang naturally. As the motion begins, the left arm lifts upward and angles inward toward the center of the chest, forming a high blocking position. The right arm bends and stays close to the torso. The head and torso remain facing forward. The motion ends with the left arm held steadily in the raised position.

The body stands upright with both arms bent near the torso. The motion begins as both arms pull inward toward the chest, with the elbows drawing close to the ribs. After briefly holding this closed position, the right arm extends sharply forward while the left arm remains folded. The motion ends with the right arm retracting and both arms returning to guard.

From a standing posture, the left arm hangs low while the right arm is bent near the chest. The motion begins as the left arm lifts upward across the front of the torso into a high blocking position. Immediately after, the torso rotates slightly to the right while the right arm extends forward. The motion ends as the torso faces forward again and both arms bend inward.

The body stands with both feet planted and both arms bent. The motion begins as the right knee lifts slightly forward and pauses. While the knee remains lifted, the left arm extends forward and then retracts. After that, the right leg lowers back to the ground. The motion ends with both arms held in guard.

From a standing position, both arms hang loosely. The motion begins as both arms swing upward and cross tightly in front of the upper torso. After holding the crossed position, the arms separate downward, with the right arm extending forward while the left arm drops close to the body. The motion ends with both arms bent near the torso.

The body stands upright with the right arm bent and the left arm relaxed. The motion begins as the torso rotates to the left while the right arm pulls backward rather than extending. After the rotation stops, the right arm suddenly extends forward. The motion ends with the torso returning to face forward.

From a stable standing posture, both arms are raised in front of the upper torso. The motion begins as the right arm lowers downward into a low blocking position while the left arm stays raised. After the block is formed, the left arm extends forward while the right arm remains low. The motion ends with both arms bending inward.

The body stands upright with both arms bent. The motion begins as the torso tilts slightly forward while neither arm moves. After the torso stops, the right arm extends forward and immediately retracts. The motion ends with the torso returning upright and both arms held in guard.

From a standing posture, the left leg remains planted while the right leg lifts backward rather than forward. While the leg is lifted, both arms move inward toward the chest. The right leg then lowers back to the ground. The motion ends with the arms returning to a guarded position.

The body stands with both arms bent at chest height. The motion begins as the left arm extends forward slowly while the right arm stays completely still. After the left arm reaches full extension, it retracts suddenly. The motion ends with both arms bent close to the torso.

From a standing position, both arms hang naturally. The motion begins as the right arm lifts straight upward alongside the head. After holding this raised position, the right arm sweeps downward across the front of the torso. The motion ends with the right arm lowered and the left arm unchanged.

The body stands upright with both arms bent. The motion begins as both arms extend forward at the same time but stop halfway. After briefly holding this incomplete extension, both arms retract fully. The motion ends with the arms folded near the torso.

From a stable standing posture, the right leg lifts sideways slightly and pauses. While the leg remains lifted, the left arm crosses inward toward the chest. The right leg then lowers back to the ground. The motion ends with both arms bent and held in guard.

The body stands upright with both arms bent. The motion begins as the torso rotates left while both arms stay fixed in place. After the rotation stops, the right arm extends forward. The motion ends with the torso rotating back and the arm retracting.

From a standing posture, the left arm is bent high while the right arm hangs low. The motion begins as the left arm lowers slowly while the right arm lifts upward. The two arms pass each other at chest height. The motion ends with the right arm raised and the left arm lowered.

The body stands with both feet apart and both arms bent. The motion begins as the right leg lifts forward slightly and holds. While the leg remains lifted, the torso rotates gently to the right. The motion ends as the torso returns forward and the leg lowers.

From a standing position, both arms hang loosely. The motion begins as the left arm extends forward while the right arm pulls backward at the same time. After both reach full range, they reverse directions and return inward. The motion ends with both arms bent.

The body stands upright with both arms bent. The motion begins as both arms rise upward together and stop near the head. After holding this position, the right arm drops downward while the left arm remains raised. The motion ends with the arms in different heights.

From a stable standing posture, the torso rotates to the right while both arms remain folded near the chest. After the rotation stops, both arms extend forward together. The motion ends as the arms retract and the torso returns forward.

The body stands with both arms bent and held close. The motion begins as the right arm extends diagonally downward instead of forward. After reaching the lowest point, the arm retracts. The motion ends with both arms bent in guard.

From a standing posture, the left leg lifts forward slightly while the right leg remains planted. While the leg is lifted, the right arm extends forward and the left arm retracts. The motion ends as the leg lowers and both arms bend inward.

The body stands upright with both arms bent. The motion begins as the torso leans slightly to the left while the arms remain still. After the lean stops, the left arm extends forward. The motion ends with the torso returning upright and the arm retracting.

From a standing position, both arms hang at the sides. The motion begins as both arms lift outward to the sides and stop at shoulder height. After holding this wide position, both arms move inward and cross in front of the torso. The motion ends with the arms folded.

The body stands with both arms bent. The motion begins as the right arm pulls backward while the left arm extends forward. After reaching opposite extremes, both arms reverse direction and return inward. The motion ends with both arms bent.

From a stable standing posture, the right leg lifts sideways and pauses. While the leg remains lifted, the right arm crosses inward toward the chest. The motion ends as the leg lowers and the arm retracts.

The body stands upright with both arms bent near the torso. The motion begins as both arms extend downward rather than forward, stopping near the hips. After holding this position, both arms bend upward again. The motion ends in a guarded stance.

From a standing posture, the torso rotates slightly left while both arms stay low. After the rotation stops, both arms lift upward together in front of the torso. The motion ends as the torso faces forward and the arms bend inward.

The body slowly squats down with both arms hanging naturally. After pausing briefly at the lowest point, it gradually stands back up. Once fully upright, the right foot steps half a step forward, and the body then returns to the initial standing posture.

Start from a standing position with arms naturally hanging down and legs together. Quickly alternate jumping forward with both feet, simulating a hopscotch-like motion, with arms tightly at the sides of the body. Finally, stand steady, keeping an upright position.

Start from a standing position with legs together and arms naturally hanging down. Quickly alternate jumping with both legs, performing a rapid stepping rhythm, with arms swinging to match the rhythm. Then, jump both legs outward to the sides, and finally return to the standing position with arms naturally hanging down.

Start from a standing position with slightly bent knees and arms naturally hanging down. Squat down and touch the ground with both hands. Then, quickly push off with the legs to stand up, raising both arms above the head. Finally, lower the arms and return to the standing position, relaxing the legs.

Start from a standing position with legs together and arms naturally hanging down. Alternately jump with both legs in small, quick jumps while extending the arms forward. Finally, land on both feet and return to the standing position, placing the arms back naturally.

Start from a standing position with arms naturally hanging down and legs together. Perform rapid small jumps forward and backward on the spot, with arms swinging from side to side. Finally, return to a standing position with arms naturally hanging down.

Starting from an upright position, the upper body rotates to the left while both feet remain fixed. After reaching the maximum rotation, the body pauses for one second, then rotates back to the neutral position and adjusts posture to regain stability.

Starting from a standing position, the person bends forward at the waist, keeping the legs straight. The hands reach toward the ground, stopping just before touching the floor. Then the torso slowly rises back to a standing position, with the hands moving upward and eventually returning to the sides.

The person begins by sitting on the invisible chair with feet flat on the floor. The body leans slightly forward while the hands rest on the knees. After a brief pause, the person pushes through the legs to stand, lifting the body up. Once upright, the person takes a small step backward with the right foot, adjusting the posture to a standing position with both hands by the side of the body.

The body descends slowly, bending at the knees and hips as if lowering to pick something up. After a brief pause, the legs straighten, and the arms rise upward before bringing the body to a fully standing position.

The body begins in an upright position, with the arms extended outward at shoulder height. The torso bends at the waist as the body lowers into a squat. At the lowest point, the arms are pulled inward toward the chest. After a brief pause, the body rises back up, extending the arms outward again, and the torso returns to the original neutral stance.

Start from a standing position with legs together and body slightly leaned forward. Begin stepping forward. Then, swing both arms quickly behind the body and perform a backflip. Finally, land and stabilize in the original position.

Start from a standing position with legs apart and arms naturally hanging down. Bend the knees slightly and quickly squat down, placing hands on the ground to perform a forward roll. After the roll, land on the feet, and quickly rise back to a standing position.

Start from a standing position with arms naturally hanging down and feet together. Begin swinging both arms at the sides of the body, mimicking the motion of jumping rope, with legs following and jumping in sync. Finally, land steadily, return the arms to the sides, and return to the standing position.

Start from a standing position with feet shoulder-width apart and arms hanging naturally. Then, raise both arms straight above the head while simultaneously jumping to spread the legs wider, then jump again to bring the feet together while lowering the arms back to the sides. Finally, remain standing still with the arms resting at the sides and feet together.

Start from a standing position with feet together and arms at the sides. Then, step the right foot far to the right side while lifting both arms to shoulder height at the sides, then pull the right foot back to center while lowering the arms. Finally, stand still with feet together and arms hanging naturally at the sides.

Start from a standing position with arms hanging naturally and feet together. Then, rotate the head slowly to look over the right shoulder while lifting the left arm to point forward, and then rotate the head back to the center while lowering the arm. Finally, stand straight with the head facing forward and arms resting at the sides.

Start from a standing position with arms naturally hanging down and feet together. Then, lift the right knee toward the chest while swinging the left arm forward and the right arm backward. Finally, lower the right leg to the ground and return to a neutral standing position with arms at the sides.

Start from a standing position with arms hanging naturally and feet together. Then, rotate the torso to the right while extending both arms outward at shoulder height. Finally, rotate the torso back to the center and drop the arms back to the sides.

Start from a standing position with feet together and arms at the sides. Then, take a large step forward with the right leg into a slight crouch while reaching both arms forward to shoulder level. Finally, push back with the right leg to return to the initial standing position with arms hanging down.

Start from a standing position with feet together and arms naturally hanging down. Then, tilt the head toward the left shoulder while lifting both elbows out to the sides at chest height. Finally, straighten the head and lower the elbows back to the sides of the torso.

Start from a standing position with arms raised straight above the head and feet shoulder-width apart. Then, bend the torso forward at the waist while lowering the arms to touch the shins. Finally, slowly lift the torso back to an upright position and lower the arms to hang naturally at the sides.

Start from a standing position with feet together and arms hanging at the sides. Then, step the left leg out to the side while simultaneously raising both arms to shoulder height to form a T-shape. Finally, step the left leg back to the center and lower both arms back to the sides.

Start from a standing position with feet together and arms hanging naturally. Then, kick the right leg forward reaching a medium height while swinging the left arm forward to meet it. Finally, retract the right leg to the starting position and bring both arms back down to the sides.

Start from a standing position with feet together and arms at the sides. Then, rotate the head slowly to look over the right shoulder while simultaneously raising the right arm to point toward the right. Finally, turn the head back to the center and lower the right arm to the side.

Start from a standing position with arms at the sides and feet together. Then, lift the right knee high while swinging the left arm forward, followed by lifting the left knee high and swinging the right arm forward in a marching motion. Finally, lower both feet to the ground and bring both arms back to the sides.

Start from a standing position with arms hanging naturally and feet shoulder-width apart. Then, raise both arms above the head while simultaneously jumping to spread the legs wider, then jump again to bring the feet together while lowering the arms. Finally, stand still with arms hanging naturally and feet together.

Start from a standing position with arms at the sides. Then, step forward with the right leg into a deep bend while extending both arms straight out to the sides for balance. Finally, push back with the right leg to return to the initial standing position and lower the arms.

Start from a standing position with feet together and arms hanging down. Then, slowly rotate the torso to the right while reaching the left arm across the chest, then rotate the torso to the left while reaching the right arm across the chest. Finally, return the torso to the center and let both arms hang naturally.

Start from a standing position with arms down and feet shoulder-width apart. Then, raise both arms straight above the head while stepping the right leg out to the side, and then pull the arms back down to the sides while bringing the right leg back to the center. Finally, stand still with arms naturally hanging down and feet together.

Start from a standing position with arms at the sides and legs together. Then, rotate the torso slowly to the left while keeping the arms extended outward at shoulder height, followed by rotating the torso back to the right. Finally, lower the arms and return to a neutral standing position with legs together.

Start from a standing position with arms at the sides and feet together. Then, tilt the head to the right shoulder while lifting the left arm to a right angle at the elbow, followed by tilting the head to the left and lowering the arm. Finally, return the head to a centered position and stand with both arms hanging naturally.

Start from a standing position with arms hanging down. Then, tilt the head to the right while lifting the left leg out to the side and raising the right arm above the head. Finally, straighten the head, lower the arm, and bring the leg back to a neutral standing stance.

The person begins by raising both arms straight above the head while standing still. After a brief pause, the arms are lowered to the sides as the right leg lifts to bring the knee toward the chest. Finally, the person lowers the right leg to the floor and tilts the head slowly to the left and then back to center.

Starting from a neutral stance, the person extends the left arm forward at shoulder height. Beginning in a standing position, the person lifts both heels off the ground to balance on the balls of the feet. While maintaining this lift, the person shrugs both shoulders upward toward the ears. The person begins by lifting their right knee toward their chest while balancing on the left leg. Starting from a neutral stance, the person tilts their head toward the left shoulder and then rolls it forward to the right shoulder. The person begins by raising both arms straight above the head while standing tall. Then, they slowly lower their arms to their sides while simultaneously lifting the right knee toward the chest. Starting from a standing position, the person leans the torso forward at the waist while extending the left leg straight back for balance. After holding this pose, they pull the torso back up to a vertical position and bring the left leg forward to tap the floor in front. The motion ends with the person raising both hands to chest height and then dropping them back to their sides.

A person stands upright then slowly lifts both arms until they are parallel to the ground while simultaneously stepping the left foot forward. After holding this pose, the arms lower back to the sides as the left foot returns to the starting position. Finally, the person tilts their head toward the right shoulder and then returns it to a neutral centered position.

The person begins by extending their left arm straight forward and then slowly rotating the entire upper body to the right while keeping the arm extended. The person begins by tilting their head slowly toward the left shoulder while keeping the rest of the body still. The person begins by raising both arms straight above the head while standing still. Then, they slowly lower their arms to their sides while simultaneously lifting the right knee toward the chest. The person initiates the movement by bending both elbows to bring their hands near their shoulders. The person starts by slowly tilting their torso forward from the waist while keeping their legs straight. The person stands upright and slowly raises both arms until they are level with the shoulders. Maintaining the arm height, they step the left foot out to the side into a wide stance, then pull the foot back and lower both arms to the sides.

From a standing position, the person lifts their right knee toward the chest while keeping both arms extended outward for balance. They hold the pose briefly before lowering the leg back to the floor and tilting their head to the right side.

The person starts by leaning their torso forward and reaching both hands toward the floor. After a short pause, they straighten back up to a neutral standing position and immediately raise their left arm straight up toward the ceiling.

At the end, the left leg crosses behind the right leg to a resting point, while the right leg lowers the heel and becomes fully stationary.

Then, the left leg extends forward into the air, while the right leg performs a shallow bend at the knee to lower the body slightly. Finally, the left leg returns to the floor in a wide stance, while the right leg straightens and shifts its weight toward the center.

Next, the left leg extends forward in mid-air as the right leg performs a small hop to maintain balance. Finally, the left leg slowly lowers to the floor while the right leg stands still in its original position.

To finish, the left arm drops straight down to the side while the right arm returns to a relaxed vertical hanging position.
